acceptance: Red first: TestLoop_MaxCyclesExit_ClearsCompletedMarker passes when the disk guard reports low disk
No cmd/evolve unit test reads the real host disk through looppreflight.DiskGuard
A disk-guard pause in RunCycleStart emits one signal with the free percent and the path

consumed.resolution: done: PR #1599 (tests never read the host disk; a disk pause is a HOST_DISK_LOW signal bounded by max_pause_s) landed in batch PR #1604 at main 30915d28c

fix: Give the loop tests a stub DiskGuard (or a nil guard) through the existing test deps (installStubDeps), so no unit test reads the host disk. Add a guard test that fails when a cmd/evolve test reaches the production DiskGuard. When RunCycleStart pauses on disk, emit one signal with the free percent, so an ACS timeout shows the disk cause.
routed_reason: blocker B1a (2026-11-20): the console built the fix in PR #1599 (disk guard: HOST_DISK_LOW, max_pause_s, tests never read the host disk); it lands in the boundary-183 batch
summary: In wave 182 cycles 2547, 2548, 2550 and 2551 failed ACS with 40 reds each. The ACS scope acs/regression/cycle1270 runs TestC1270_003, which runs TestLoop_MaxCyclesExit_ClearsCompletedMarker in cmd/evolve. That test calls runLoop, and dispatchSequentialCycle calls looppreflight.RunCycleStart with the production DiskGuard. The host had 2.6% free disk, under the 5% pause line, so RunCycleStart waited in 15 s steps for ever (goroutine dump: looppreflight.waitForInterval at cyclestart.go:51). The nested go test used the whole 10 min ACS Go lane budget, and every later scope was not run. The same test passes in 0.96 s after the console freed disk. The failure classifier said infra-systemic but did not name the disk.
title: Loop tests call the real disk guard, so a host under 5% free disk hangs them until the ACS Go lane budget expires
